arguments.name: Conditional Reynolds anomalous-perception argument
arguments.position: Strongest selected positive case; project reconstruction
premises: Carter reproduces visual tool/case details and relatives imagery substantially through Sabom, with additional documentary wording.
Carter places early checkable perceptions before absent brainstem responses; Hameroff’s phase agreement is explicitly conditional.
Carter quotes Cordova as monitoring in the adjacent operating room and requesting an exact-parameter experiment.
Carter uses visual specificity, sealing/masking and unreported clicks to challenge ordinary hearing and reconstruction.
Woerlee’s rejoinder accepts Carter’s distinction between a measurable BAER and conscious hearing, and rejects Hameroff’s monitoring characterization.
Smit reports running the sound demonstration: clicks were intolerable, yet ambient sounds remained audible and speech worsened with tighter headphones.
Smit argues that unbearable clicks would have been remembered, so their absence from Reynolds’ accounts supports nonphysical hearing.
bridge_principles: Independently established accurate acquisition during specified exclusion conditions would challenge an ordinary-channel explanation.
Narrative phase assignment must coincide with independently verified acquisition timing; vividness alone cannot supply it.
arguments.conclusion: Visual specificity and the disputed monitoring/hearing setup motivate investigation, but this packet does not establish excluded-process acquisition.
arguments.strongest_objection: Early checkable phases are not the absent-brainstem/arrest interval; retrospective report and incomplete information controls allow ordinary hearing/reconstruction alternatives.
arguments.strongest_reply: The later technical details, conscious-hearing distinction and missing click reports challenge an unqualified assertion that ordinary hearing has been demonstrated.

arguments.name: Conditional ordinary-process account and its correction
arguments.position: Strongest selected direct critic and actual replies
premises: Woerlee proposes awareness plus drug effects, using related surgical protocols to supplement Sabom’s nontechnical account.
Woerlee’s addendum prescribes a consumer sound demonstration, acknowledges unmatched pulse control and unknown earpiece attenuation, then asserts audibility.
Hameroff disclaims case expertise, conditionally permits awareness, and challenges missing BAER results while calling BAER a definitive monitor.
Woerlee’s rejoinder accepts Carter’s distinction between a measurable BAER and conscious hearing, and rejects Hameroff’s monitoring characterization.
The rejoinder describes actual MLAEP use in Reynolds as likely despite its absence from the cited Spetzler article.
The rejoinder defends a possible physical account but explicitly leaves the immaterial explanation unexcluded because case data are insufficient.
The rejoinder infers combined lack of pain and anxiety from separate reported symptom percentages.
Carter’s further reply targets points 5 and 6, accepts point 3, and does not develop answers to points 1,2 and4.
Carter objects that the pain/anxiety margins do not establish their intersection, and emphasizes phenomenological differences.
Given only n=25, pain=7 and anxiety/stress=9, the count reporting neither can range from 9 to16.
Smit’s quoted Key and Prescott reports include partial conversation and clear television speech, respectively, with setup differences.
bridge_principles: Evidence that a mechanism can occur under relevant conditions is distinct from evidence it actually produced this report.
Related surgical protocols do not by themselves fix this patient’s monitoring or drug state.
arguments.conclusion: The ordinary-process account remains a live alternative; Woerlee’s rejoinder narrows the evidential conclusion and does not exclude the rival.
arguments.strongest_objection: Carter/Smit contest acoustic equivalence, subjective character and inferential moves from monitoring/marginal symptoms.
arguments.strongest_reply: Woerlee distinguishes bone from air conduction and acknowledges BAER is not conscious hearing; Smit’s own reported results include some hearing. Neither decides the case mechanism.

arguments.name: Demonstration, dependence and extrapolation limits
premises: The 25 awareness descriptions and 19,575 surgical denominator are reproduced from Sebel by the disputants, not a Reynolds sample.
Smit reports running the sound demonstration: clicks were intolerable, yet ambient sounds remained audible and speech worsened with tighter headphones.
Smit’s quoted Key and Prescott reports include partial conversation and clear television speech, respectively, with setup differences.
Smit’s Spring2012 letter includes May and June2012 material alongside an April2 posting statement.
Carter’s further reply says the proposed institutional hearing test had not received Woerlee’s response and would exclude heavy anesthesia.
The proposed test, Smit’s performed demonstration and an actual calibrated case-equivalent experiment are different evidential states.
The provisional later Woerlee Successful Test webpage remains uninspected after a stopped access route; its title supplies no outcome.
The strongest positive and ordinary-process arguments remain conditional because timing, prefeedback information controls and calibrated case data are incomplete.
Later replies add discussion of one Reynolds event; they do not establish irreversible-death survival, cosmic consciousness, timelessness or consciousness-caused recovery.
bridge_principles: A demonstration using different equipment/participants/drug state does not automatically reproduce a clinical event.
One narrator/event and repeated reports remain one dependence group.
Temporary or conditional independence does not entail same-person survival beyond irreversible death or universal/timeless consciousness.
arguments.conclusion: The packet can revise source/reply coverage and technical attributions while leaving all twelve stronger-conclusion gates withheld.
arguments.strongest_objection: A well-established anomaly could still be relevant to models permitting survival.
arguments.strongest_reply: Conditional relevance is preserved; timing, identity, persistence and cosmic/normative bridges require additional evidence.
